questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests end-to-end image provenance across multi-cloud GPU workloads, combining CI, runtime policies, and verification in real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Image provenance, Cosign, Sigstore, reproducible builds
- Kubernetes admission control (Kyverno/OPA)
- Buildx/OCI digests and registry security
- GPU workload constraints and cross-cloud policy

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: build, sign, verify
name: BuildSignVerify
on: [push]
jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up QEMU/Buildx
      - name: Build and push
        run: |
          docker buildx create --use
          image=registry.example.com/project/image:${{ github.sha }}
          docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
            -t $image --build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1 .
          cosign sign -key cosign.key $image
          docker push $image
      - name: Verify signature
        run: cosign verify -key cosign.pub $image
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-image
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: check-cosign-signature
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    verifyImages:
    - image: registry.example.com/*
      pattern: "^.+$"
```

```yaml

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: guest-deploy
spec:

    spec:
      containers:

```

```yaml

kind: Deployment

  name: secure-deploy
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        build.sha256: "abcdef123456..."
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/project/image:sha-abcdef
```

## Why This Is Asked

- Sigstore cosign and SLSA attestations
- Multi-cloud deployment and policy enforcement (OPA, Kyverno)

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: sign and attest serverless image
name: Sign and Attest Serverless Images
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  sign_attest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          IMAGE=registry.example.com/function-${{ github.sha }}:latest
          docker build -t $IMAGE .
      - name: Sign image
        run: cosign sign --key cosign.key $IMAGE
      - name: Attest image
        run: cosign attest --key cosign.key --predicate attest.json $IMAGE
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a reject-by-default policy for hostPath usage, a common attack surface, and to describe how to maintain a dynamic allowlist in production.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- hostPath volumes and host filesystem access risk
- dynamic allowlist via a ConfigMap and a small controller to sync data
- CI validation (dry-run, gatekeeper admissions) and runtime validation

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: HostPathPolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: HostPathConstraint
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package hostpathpolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i in input.review.object.spec.volumes
        input.review.object.spec.volumes[i].hostPath
        not data.hostpath_allowlist.namespaces[_]
        msg := "hostPath volumes are forbidden unless in allowlist"
      }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: HostPathConstraint
metadata:
  name: hostpath-deny
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: ["v1"]
      kinds: ["Pod"]
```

Compliant manifest (no hostPath):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23
```

Noncompliant manifest (hostPath present):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
  namespace: default
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: data
    hostPath:
      path: /var/lib/data
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /data
      name: data
```

CI/runtime validation plan: run Gatekeeper admission checks on PRs, simulate allowed namespaces via the ConfigMap sync, and perform a runtime audit post-deploy using a test pod to verify policy enforcement.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CI policy enforcement skills using image signing—a common real-world requirement in production Kubernetes environments. It assesses understanding of supply chain security and GitOps practices.

## Key Concepts
- Container image signing with cosign
- Public key infrastructure for signature verification
- Manifest scanning in CI pipelines
- Handling signed vs. unsigned images in deployment gates
- GitOps workflow security

## Code Example

**GitHub Actions Workflow:**
```yaml
name: Verify Image Signatures
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'manifests/**'

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Extract image references
        id: images
        run: |
          echo "images=$(grep -roh 'registry.example.com/[^"]+' manifests/ | sort -u | jq -R -s -c '. | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          for image in $(echo '${{ steps.images.outputs.images }}' | jq -r '.[]'); do
            cosign verify --key cosign.pub $image
          done
```

**Sample Manifest (signed image):**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: myapp
        image: registry.example.com/myapp:v1.0.0
```

**Failing Manifest (unsigned):**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
```

- Namespace isolation: tenant label validation, per-tenant RBAC bindings
- Security: Istio mTLS (PeerAuthentication), NetworkPolicy for egress control
- CI verification: conftest for policy testing, kubeval for manifest validation, dry-run kubectl apply

## CI Verification Steps
1. **Policy Validation**: Use `conftest test k8s-manifests/ -p policy.rego` to verify compliance
2. **Manifest Validation**: Run `kubeval manifests/*.yaml` against Kubernetes schemas
3. **Dry Run**: Execute `kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f manifests/` to test admission
4. **Network Policy Test**: Use `kubectl get networkpolicy -n <tenant-ns>` to verify egress restrictions
5. **ServiceAccount Audit**: Check `kubectl auth can-i --as=<serviceaccount> <verb> <resource>` for least privilege

This comprehensive approach ensures every namespace meets security requirements before deployment, with automated CI gates preventing policy violations.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question probes policy-as-code skills, Istio security posture, and CI/CD integration. It tests ability to craft minimal, verifiable manifests and to reason about runtime vs CI checks.

## Key Concepts

- Istio PeerAuthentication mtls: STRICT
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno policy or alternative
- CI validation: lint, dry-run apply, policy testing
- Runtime enforcement: Istio sidecars enforce mTLS

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate sample
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8smtlstrict
spec:
  crd:
    Spec:
      groups: ["constraints.gatekeeper.sh"]
      names:
        kind: K8sMTLSStrict
        plural: k8smTLSStricts
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8smtlstrict
        violation["mtls_missing"] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Namespace"
          not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["istio-injection"]
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sMTLSStrict
metadata:
  name: mtls-strict
spec:
  match:
    requiredImages: []
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest: PeerAuthentication with mtls: STRICT
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: default
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest: missing PeerAuthentication
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample
  namespace: test
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: sample
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: sample
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
```
